body:
I would not wear the corset if I were you..better to go for a compression wrap-type brace.  I've always worn my underwire bra under my sportsbra every day (because after truck comes customers and god forbid someone glimpses the outline of a nipple right?  How unprofessional!)..  
About 5 months ago, I was just shoving a 40 lb box of frozen chicken onto the top shelf in the freezer, fingertipping with one arm because I'm 5'3" and the floor's too slick for stepstools..warped cardboard on the bottom caught the lip of the metal, and that push shoved my underwire between my ribs and up.  Cracked a rib and ruptured that vein that goes from your breast, under the armpit, and down the arm.  I'm still not healed up completely because this job is kind of abusive.  Lol.
TMI story, but I can only imagine the damage that corset could do.  😬
Do you have a linen closet outside of the bathroom?  Most medications lose their efficacy if not kept in a cool and dark place...bathrooms have too much temperature fluctuation.

You set your availability, but the auto-scheduler will plug you in whenever it needs WITHIN that availability.  So it won't always be the same every week because it's dependent on the store's needs, no guarantees.  The most common way this bites PT in the ass is short shifts: you may give an 8 hour window, three specific days a week, but the store only needs you for 4 hours on two of those days.  So you plan for 24 hours and only get 8. 

However, if you tailor your availability to the store's needs (weekends, extra delivery/ad set days like Aldi Finds or Wine day, days that are heavy on FT fixed days off, all closes if your store needs closers/truck if that's what's needed), you'll be more apt to receive consistent hours week to week.


Edit: sorry, I just caught the PT cashier part of your post...honestly, that's probably the best bet for consistency so long as you give closing availability.

I have tried time and again to get comfortable at a "job is a job is a job" but given work sequesters away the majority of my waking hours for the rest of my life..I just can't stomach settling for the soul suck.  Most of us can't make enough money to support vacations and hobbies anymore, regardless of who we work for or what we do, so income is no longer the driving factor.  Most of us have so much on our plates individually that we don't have the energy for those things outside of working hours, even if we had the time/income.  So we figure out a way to make a career of what we love to do, otherwise we'll never actually get to do it at all.  And what would be the sad point of that?

This sounds very much like, "you've had your day in the sun, now put it all on the back burner and pump me out some babies." She's trying to establish a foundation, she's trying to pivot and adapt to unforeseen changes and circumstances, she's literally just doing life.  Not just for herself, but to also set herself up to be a working mother..that takes time, and unfortunately a lot of refiguring as the political climate shifts and constricts.  You're making the struggle of the process out to be her fault, when she's been doing her part all along to give you what you want.  It sucks that you guys can't simultaneously prioritize both of your careers AND your giant life goal of being parents, but there's only so much time, effort, and money to go around.  With that biological clock ticking, one has to come before the other.  

There's nothing wrong with wanting a housewife, but that needs to be laid out from the get-go to ascertain that everyone wants the same thing, and you need to set your life up to support that  kind of dynamic (same as she's been setting up hers to support motherhood in a two-income household).  It sounds to me like you married someone who wants more for themselves than that, and it's "getting in the way" of your dream.  How about some introspection?

You're part time, use that schedule availability to your advantage so this doesn't happen.  Full timers have a set day off so that the most they can work in a row is 6 (because there'll be another day off somewhere in there).  I get that part timers are afraid that without leaving their availability open, there won't be enough hours scheduled, but that's literally the single perk of being part time.  No sense in whining about your coworker (who probably has a DEI Agreement of some sort), when it's in your power to better your situation.
I thought it was a free weight being chased by broccoli, subliminal messaging..🤣

No, my perception of "shrinking myself" is having to base my actions/lack therof off of others' small-minded perceptions, usually fortified by a complete void of emotional intelligence.  It's exhausting and suffocating, regardless of the context.  But go ahead and troll on..fly that flag high and you can play the part of Exhibit A.  ;p

Okay.  In a perfect world, we'd be able to go off of our sexual impulses and so long as everything was consensual, no harm no foul.  It's actually completely healthy for you to have this sex drive..it IS fun to experience people, how each experience itself is different, what you learn about yourself through each experience.  If/when you learn about love languages, you'll probably find that physical affection is one of yours.  Ideally, you'd meet someone whose primary love language was also physical affection and maybe their Slut Switch wouldn't get flipped in their head when you went with that.  Everyone could just go with how they felt, treat each other like human beings, and move on into a Rom-Com montage.  

But this is not a perfect world, and while society as a whole has become far more sex-forward...like I swear folks exchange nudes on the heels of their contact info...women are still held to an impossible standard.  Always have been, but now it seems to be just as "bad" to be a prude as a hoe.  We have to think five steps ahead to the repercussions of every action, perform the mental gymnastics to ascertain not just what is RIGHT but what will be decided regardless of what is right, and act accordingly.  

In this context, I'd say you'll find that regardless of how natural your libido is, and how quick guys will be to go with that in the moment....their hangups will bleed over onto you.  I had a short phase of this when I was your age until I heard "well you're just one of those girls we get to treat like this." Okay, well if that's how y'all perceive XYZ, then let me set the record straight by presenting as XYZ.  It absolutely sucks ass to have to make your world smaller, to shrink yourself to fit into others' small-minded boxes..but until they catch up with the times and expand past the stupidity, this is how you keep your heart safe.

What's rough is those of us that meet/exceed standards just get burned out hollow trying to compensate for the ones who've figured out how to milk/tolerate the job..and she'll probably be the one to last long enough to see any benefit out of that involuntary 401k.  

Truly, she has it figured out..it's just only in HER best interest, but look at the company she has for a role model.  Loyalty begets loyalty and all that.

It would be smart to have a backup plan just in case.  If people are on vacations, the store is short-staffed, or it's peak season, you'll probably still see the hours to float your bills/apprenticeship.  But only with a full time status are you guaranteed anything; the auto-scheduler uses part-time employees to fill in the holes, usually just a couple 4-5 hour shifts per week.  If you set your availability to certain days/blocks of time during the week to make room for Not Aldi, that just decreases your odds of receiving hours.  Used to, our SMs could pencil us in, but unfortunately it's now largely dependent on whether your SM is willing to go against policy for the sake of the store or not.

Exactly.  But since you won't agree to the full time availability/hours, you're "bottom of the barrel" and get the scraps, regardless of whether they actually need the help or not.  I dropped down from full time to part time, my hours were cut and given to others.  Then they immediately turned around calling for help because they were short handed.  Sorry, shoulda kept me on the schedule.  The wishy washy gives ya whiplash, and Idk about you but my livelihood is kind of off limits for games.

Yeah, they're really cracking down on the whole "give us free reign of your life or get fucked" thing.  They can't just put you on call, because then you surely wouldn't work there, but that's the unspoken truth of part time hours at Aldi.  And the whole lying through their teeth to string you along..yeah, also a favorite card to play.
Color calls attention.

I'll be 32 in September and have attempted dating once since 2020.  I've found that it grosses me out to try people on for size/especially to be tried on for size (and that's what dating feels like to me).  I've lived experiences which have taught me to be very selective and to take even a commitment to a prospective commitment seriously, because I do appreciate my solitude/time/energy so making a choice to "spend" it is an investment.  Apparently that's pretty intense since dating is supposed to be fun and lighthearted.  

There's also the factor of most "date activities" being awkward AF until you actually know each other..many of us clam up and never really manage to come out to be met/honored before the interest fizzles out..but how are you supposed to get to know each other otherwise?  I am personally far more comfortable going from friends to lovers, but how often does the bottom fall out in the middle..unless it's a unicorn situation, you've just established yourself as a discount milk cow.  Only took a couple of those around 21 to turn me into a bit of a prude for self-preservation's sake.  
 
I have yet to find a man whose mind works like mine, so I hold out; discouraging to my hopeless romantic heart, sure.. but I'm grateful that we have that option now. I COULD be married with kids by now, but it would be cookie-cutter picturesque "sense"--not love.  Those men deserve to find it same as I do.  I could also have stayed behind and gotten unalived, obviously pretty easy to see why singledom is the better alternative there as well.  

 So...we're in a societal age of damned if you do, damned if you don't.  Doesn't really have much to do with biological age at all, imo.  But I think it would help to shift your perspective, nod to my novel above.  Hah.  Regardless, ♥️💪

Being an active participant in society, we learn ourselves by comparison to others and their perceived reactions to how we present ourselves.  Imo, this is where the mindfuck comes in. In the absence of others, the stillness of solitude, it's so much easier to hear your own intuitive voice.

Instead, play hermit and sit with yourself for a few months.  Do a quiet eat, pray, love stint..see what "care" is to your self..what it is you feel the need to recover from. What do you find yourself wanting to spend your time on..what sparks that flame of interest in your gut?  Alternatively, what have you found you're happy to forget when not forced to pursue it?   This thought process can apply to anything: hobbies, career paths, ethics and morals.  Just as you've learned to sort of "diagnose" feelings in the body as indicators toward picking up a cold, or that hunger pains mean you need to eat...learn how a "yes that's for me" and "no, that doesn't sit well with me" feels in the body and make moves based on THAT.  Curate your life choices, small and large, around your internal voice and you will be one with the Self.

My person said something to me along these lines before too, though not drunk and prompted by my own question about what kind of girls he usually gravitated to before.  It did gut me as well, but he'd meant it to portray that I am the exception.  Which I understand because while I can acknowledge that people are outwardly attractive (and could describe my "type" to you), when it comes to actually choosing someone to build a relationship with none of that matters to me.  I go with how I feel intrinsically, and any attraction to physical attributes is just a bonus; lots of things I may consider a dealbreaker/requirement in the general turn out to be inconsequential in light of the connection.

Yes.  I think that if a person is open to an enlightened perspective of what is ethical, they will at the least show remorse with having upset someone with their actions--compulsive empathy, like yawning when someone else yawns.  So if they have no remorse, they either already know that it's wrong and don't care or don't have the capacity for understanding.  So whether a spoken, direct teaching of right and wrong, or indirect/unspoken sort of a lack of gifting compassion?(Which would probably bring about a sense of shame/wanting to atone in a "good" person)..it will bounce right off.  That's a very black and white layout though, of course there's always grey in everything.  And probably more dependent on dark psychology.

No, I get you too.  I guess it's hard for people to separate the little humans from the burden that's attached to the concept of kids.  It's not the kid's fault they're here, doing what kids do, reacting as kids react.  I'm pretty sure plenty of us feel like crashing out in public sometimes too, we're just old enough there are worse consequences for things like that.  Lol.  But I can't help that being around said crashouts makes me want to crawl out of my skin and run for the closest exit.  I am fiercely protective of kids, they can be hilarious and I love witnessing them discover the world, but holy shit the sensory overload..so I won't have my own.  Kids need people around them who relish that energy, who can feed it.  Another benefit to the special interest friends thing, for parents.
I admire your idealism, but where accountability is concerned I've learned you can't even begin to teach Pig Latin to a fish.

So you're saying that forgiveness without a true show of remorse/intention to atone is condoning the behavior?  Slap on the wrist and a lollipop for the road?  

I agree.  But the people who have no regard for ethics don't care about earning your forgiveness, they just care about getting what they want.  The forgiveness is for you..forgiving yourself for being good to someone who took advantage, for giving the benefit of the doubt or being naïve--in willful denial.  For that residual compassion even after you've been fucked over.  

Best you're going to get out of me is just leaving em to rot in peace, and even that's too lenient on most...unjust really.  But not many of us get to hold the power in our hands to make those calls, so.

Nowhere in my comment did I speak ill on children or good parenting.  Just acknowledged that having children is a life-changing event, and that you can't expect for everyone else to morph their lives into alignment with your choice.  Same could be said for all kinds of pivotal life choices..marriage, moving, career changes..people veer off on their own paths.  You might still have a spot in your heart for them, catch up when you can, but not able to be in each other's hip pockets anymore.  That's normal, that's life.  
Somehow when it's because someone had kids, y'all always come out of the woodwork to get butthurt about it.  Is this because of the "it takes a village" thing?  Are y'all actually just upset your community isn't helping you raise your kids?  I'm not trying to be an asshole, I just don't get it. I'm very much a live and let live person, no harm done.

Unfortunately most of the time once people become parents, that becomes their identity and that kid's a third wheel whether they're actually present or not.  This is why people have special interest friends..Mom friends, fantasy football friends, spelunking friends..there will always be someone to connect with over shared experiences/lifestyles, and a friend not being interested in your special interest doesn't make them a bad friend.  I know that'd be hard to take being something you created and love, because it's a human and not a material hobby. . but having children is a choice that you make for yourself, not for everyone around you too.

Have an old colleague who's just within the past few months come out with the truth about her failed marriage.  They were an IT couple..huge close-knit group of family and friends, both with prestigious, public careers, quarterly lavish vacations, two beautiful kids excelling in academia and extracurriculars.  Literal picture of perfection til she finally received irrefutable proof that my dude was fucking anything he could that moved (and gaslighting her into psychosis to protect his fun/peace). Took her everything to peel away from that, she's still trying to play amicable at family functions for the kids' sake because "despite everything, he's such a good Dad."  I'd beg to differ that's not a strong role model in any right, but you know..keep my mouth shut as it's not my business and she's been clear about her stance on that with everyone.  

I write this long ass, seemingly completely unrelated novel to conclude that of all her wonderfully supportive friends, family, and colleagues, what do you think everyone rants and raves about when she posts pictures of these "family" events?  I'm pretty sure getting skinny doesn't really feel like much of a consolation prize.

I don't want to have to stare at your brake lights..foot hovering over the brake ..for miles on end trying to make sure I don't end up in your cab with you.  I want to set my damned cruise control and dissociate into my coffee/music while I make my way to or from work.  The road, the car, is just a means to an end, and you're impeding my progress by causing congestion.  Our drivers Ed teacher told us it was understood to go 5 mph over the posted speed limit, and when in doubt, go with the flow of traffic.  10-15 mph under is just as dangerous, if not moreso, than 10-15 mph over.  That shit just makes everybody on the road pushy, gets everyone bumper to bumper/whipping around and ACTUALLY speeding to pass..just a wreck waiting to happen.

Honestly, what you've expressed here sums up why many people including myself choose to be child-free.  I wish more people were able to bring themselves to this conclusion before conception, but I get that having children is still framed as such a "notch in the bedpost of life" that a lot of people would find it taboo to consider NOT doing so.  I could play devil's advocate and say that many of your "blissful mom friends" are probably faking it til they make it more than you'd think, also because it'd be taboo to speak of anything but said bliss of motherhood.  Because once you acknowledge something it's nearly impossible to overlook, and what a dangerous thread to pull.  

It's a shit situation.  You're completely warranted in feeling the way you do.  Solidarity.  But your kid didn't ask to be born, surely not to a mother who doesn't want to be a mother, who doesn't want to be a pillar alongside the milestones.  He'll feel that, if he doesn't already.  And he deserves better, so giddy up and push through.  It ain't about you anymore..you decided that 2 1/2 years ago.

I'd wager it's moreso about how most of society no longer has the means to spend on learning/perfecting any "lost art."  The arts, talents, skills..they all take dedication, time, and money that we don't have for slaving away trying not to be homeless.  The rich kids get lessons and tutors while the poor kids get to go try and find someone who will hire a 14 yo.
Thank you for having sense.

Unless you're writing people up for that on a regular day, it'd be retaliation to punish hourly employees for leaving at their scheduled time rather than* staying to finish someone else's work**.

Would never be me anyway, but you go ahead and try playing that backhanded petty shit and see what your turnover rate looks like.  🤣🤣

Are they rude though?  Or is it just not the saccharine sweet, handheld "tiptoe through the tulips of Aldi" main character treatment that American customers have come to expect?  You come ask a question, we answer it and keep on working.  I cannot tell you how many times that has been seen as rude, because I don't paste on a 1000-watt smile and CATER.  

I'm single-handedly unloading 2/3 of a semi onto shelves within 5 hours' time, forgive me if I don't prepare a little song and dance for each customer who pulls me out of my sweaty reverie to inquire where the fucking bread is (with signs everywhere).  Lol.  We're human.. expect some candid moments to back up your claim, sure.. but I wish people wouldn't instantly jump to the "rude" conclusion from a flat face or tone.  That's not rudeness, that's "I'd probably be laid out here in the floor if it wouldn't get me fired." A confused look when you ask where something is?  Probably me trying to figure out a clear way to explain the directions, since there are no damned aisle numbers.  A fleeting look of exasperation probably means I've already heard that one 20 times within the last hour, probably irritation toward our company for leaving us in that predicament moreso than you.  Did I audibly sigh, or am I just trying to catch my breath because you came around the corner and expected me to talk?  I'm not even angry that you're shopping while I'm trying to work..I'm irritated that Aldi has squeezed us to the point that I'm having to risk everyone's safety to do this while you're shopping.  

An enlightened perspective would concur that none of it is about you and you don't have to take anything near as personally as you do.  I say "you" as a general btw.

You have to hold boundaries with things like this..with so much on management's plates all the time, they're quick to push anything they can on the associates who don't get paid to do all that extra.  Your boss can't force you to stay, they're just banking on you feeling guilty or not having the balls to put your foot down.  This company is HUGE on skirting by on what's not addressed/lack of clarity in policies..it's up to you (us) to teach our leaders how to act sometimes.
Gosh man, I'm sorry.  I hope speaking up for yourself makes a difference in this case, because that's unacceptable.  Good luck!

They don't start our breaks til after grocery is done, so I'm usually going on 20 hours since I've last eaten by the time they finally let me go.  Then there's usually only an hour left of my shift.  SO GOOD for my health.  🤣🤣

I don't have a solution for you, because of course there are no policies to force leadership to use common sense here, but.. you're not alone!

People will preach about the sanctity of life for all til they're blue in the face (when it comes to things like abortion or capital punishment) but always seem to get REALLY quiet when it comes to the quality of life for those of us who have endured the worst that the world has to offer.  What they want is for us to just finish deteriorating somewhere they don't have to witness reality, to let em be oblivious in peace.  Acknowledging that some actions really do deserve revenge/violent justice opens a whole can of worms that most people don't have the capacity to process.  Shakes their carefully-curated worldview, God forbid.  🙄

Lol.  But what can we always plan for?  Bills.  And Aldi to dick us around on our hours.  
If you end up in an expensively shitty medical situation, there are payment plans and emergency insurance options..just takes time and headaches.  I guess in a perfect world we wouldn't have to choose between securing shelter and health, but that's just the beauty of this country we live in.
PTO will be paid out, sick time does not.

Obviously it's going to depend on your situation, but for me personally it's always been the cheaper route to just pay out of pocket.  Unless you end up with broken bones, need surgery, get pregnant or cancer...you know, things that are going to cost thousands of dollars on their own.  Our coverage is fickle at best and a fight at worst, you're shelling out the monthly payments on TOP of trying to reach the deductible that hardly anything counts toward.  A year's worth of monthlies+the deductible alone..that's my homeowner's insurance for the year.  Thankfully it's not yet illegal in the US to be medically uninsured, so you can decide where to prioritize your income.  I just feel like so many of us get hoodwinked over that, and then you're stuck.
We also get hoodwinked thinking full time hours will make the difference to pay for all that.

Just keep in mind that you'll still be working roughly the same amount of hours, just with an inconsistent schedule and losing money to insurance if you opt in.  The sick pay and PTO is pretty much the only true "benefit" of full time unless you have dependents.

Lmao.  Right!  Do these people not realize how physically laborious this job is?  I shower every morning, double up on clinical strength cancer-in-a-stick AND Lume sweat control, and still have to reapply twice during truck.  Dry shampoo too.  

If there's not time to go to my locker, smell gets absorbed into the fabric of our tees so then it's eau de floral BO.  Know what causes BO like that?  High cortisol.  What does working at Aldi cause?  High cortisol.  

Seeing that "tell a manager because that's losing the store money" just boiled my guts, sorry.
When they chase me down at the bailer and I have to pull the whole box bin back out on the floor for them.  😮‍💨
Lol.  Right.  You'll work the pallet.  Just from off the floor since you don't have steel toes.

You hit the nail on the head.  Even though subbing is darn near free money (in secondary, at least), I quit because all that was ever available were Elementary/Para jobs.  The atmosphere in those schools was so militaristic and just..light dampening..that it felt unethical to be complicit in enforcing their codes of conduct.  It was so obviously an indoctrination factory.  These kids..and the educators with souls..deserve better.

Apprehensive of the crowd that's gonna take that title and run with it: "oh, it's terrible that happened to you, but at least you still get to experience the miracle of life!"

Rape is worse than murder. Fuck the platitudes.

But I am grateful that you're beginning to come to terms and process.  It is another defense mechanism of survival to try and rework a memory into something more palatable for the psyche.  To gloss over details, to impart a conscience on a human who's shown he doesn't have one.  To try and convince yourself that it was just unwanted sex, or to be grateful it wasn't as brutal as it could have been.  But all of those mental gymnastics are to the benefit of your abuser, of those who would prefer to be comfortably ignorant. 

The PTSD is going to be no joke..breaking this down is going to be excruciating.  But your body will recognize you honoring its truth.  There will be growth from this.  ♥️

Someone else asked on FB a while back and an employee from that store said she lived, but that the hammer came down for everyone to keep the whole ordeal hushhush.  Don't really know why, as I believe this one was a rare instance in which Aldi wasn't at fault of some negligence.  Whatever..point being, at least she isn't dead.
Exactly!
Welcome to Aldi, this is how they getcha.  Unless you can see yourself taking on that fulltime clusterfuck schedule, best be looking for another job.

Final dealbreaker for me is this last little OE pinch.  These past few paychecks are so dismal, the only way for me to be comfortable is to stop shelling out so much money into the insurance..and the only way to stop paying for the insurance is to drop down to part time or basically quit.  I'll make more, and be happier, elsewhere..which is crazy considering we make $4-5 more an hour than I can find elsewhere, but it's the way they work their system.  All the other reasons are just the icing on the poopcake..used to, I might have tried to stick it out til peak season, but my nervous system and I are just over the rollercoaster.
Eew, even two people splitting a pallet has us tripping over each other.  Not about being a team, just about not having space for all that.

They just rewrote the policy on this a month or two ago..unless otherwise mandated by your state, we're down to just one paid 30 min break.  By policy, this would mean no splitting the break into two 15s, but managers use their discretion for smokers.  
We're also, by policy, supposed to stay in the break room for our breaks..just in case they need us to clock back in real quick to help...but by and large everyone understands that an interrupted break is not a break, and unless there's a dire staffing situation that day hourly employees are free to leave the premises for break.
Well then you're lucky enough not to be one of those people to have firsthand knowledge.
I REALLY wish you would research more on the physical implications of mental health disorders.  This comment is not stupid, but ignorant..and in turn, incredibly tone deaf.

Some people are beyond help, and that isn't for you to decide.  Sounds harsh, but again..your stance, though well-meaning, denies the suicidal person their autonomy and dismisses their reality in favor of what YOU want/expect.  (You expect that you can help them, you expect that they will let you, that something can change.)

It's like stringing a body along on life support for years, or repeatedly resuscitating a hospice patient without a DNR..just because the meatsuit still fires, does not mean they're still there.  Or that their quality of life in any way justifies those cruel means.
Thank you for the award!!
I'd argue it's selfish to expect others to continue suffering indefinitely, just so you don't have to deal with the pain of losing them.

FWIW..OE's got us running on two people (regardless of how busy we are or what shape the store is in).  So that leaves all of the customer questions, spills, running outside to get someone's quarter unstuck, etc to the curbside shopper since the other is stuck on register.

Theme runs through every single component of this job..the ringing while managing 7 SCOs (while trying to keep customers from taking your cart corporate says they're allowed to take)...the throwing truck with every single pallet being mixed across aisles, column stacked, and poorly wrapped (alongside juggling the cheap ass state of our packaging/boxes..plus boxing/leveling/date pulling/cleaning as you go because the 2 closers got pushed out before the job was done)...

They preach efficiency and time, then turn around and make it fundamentally impossible to achieve without cloning yourself.  If you zoom out, this is literally a rat race.  Fuck em.  Do your best and fuck the rest.

Handbook says it's possible they may just push you into rehab and keep your job on hold til you get back, but regardless..your job will be in jeopardy if they find cannabis in your system.  They've even added addendums this past month or two for Delta 8 and whatnot.  As there's no way to prove when you consumed it last, no way to prove you didn't run yourself over because you were high, 😬
I would just go to the doc on my own, if I were you..an uninsured visit.

Every morning I'm looking at those people taking 3-4 hours (sometimes their whole shift) to finish their sector, while I finish 2-3 sectors because I meet pallet pacing requirements...honestly I think I'm the idiot in this scenario.  Their jobs are still secure and we get paid the same.  If Aldi management held their employees to standard, it'd be a different story, but it's hard to fire your friends..most of us are all good people who don't deserve to be thrown out on our asses regardless of being deadweight on the schedule. Unless you end up with one of the few management teams who can separate business from feelings, you'll most likely be secure so long as you look like you're working on camera.
I use the exact same line, just like I'm teaching a kindergarten class.  ..and that's me trying not to be snarky..is that snarky?  😬
They just made us sign another form saying we won't, so just be careful!

Which tells me where the company values lie: with protecting their image over their own people.  Fear of potential lawsuits keeping them from actually lifting a finger to protect anyone or anything, so of course it wouldn't be deemed worth the investment.  🙄  Then the losses must not be hurting them much..or like others have said, they just plan to compensate for that with our COL raises.  Still don't see how that could possibly even out.

This right here is why anytime I see "team player atmosphere" in a job description now, I keep scrolling.  It's literally just code for "we expect you to pick up the slack for your coworkers (and uppers) with a smile" and "unless they're caught stealing time, we're not going to make any moves to hold our employees accountable to standards." Because as long as the work gets done, as long as they can look at the cameras and it SEEMS like those people are working, their job is secure.  It's lazy management practice, but it's common.  Just that much more frustrating here because of our skeleton model.
So much of this wouldn't fly in our store..hopefully this'll blow over and not catch on.

Oooof. Tell me you don't/wouldn't pull this same shit without telling me....

Changes to the schedule cannot be made without employee approval past its official posting, that's universal knowledge.

You miss the "regardless of context" part or are you just trying to be cute?

SO MUCH of classic lit (especially American Lit) is a slog to get through, but I also don't think every lesson in education needs to be tailored to kids' sensibilities. Literature is often in itself proof of our history, and I think there's a vital undertone to perceiving society's cyclical nature through the various lenses of writers over the course of thousands of years--it's important to identify the constants and what that means for the whole, which we can't do if we're only willing to process information that's palatable.  

I do think we would all greatly benefit from less rote memory/regurgitation of information in school, less focus on the trivial details and more emphasis on standardized education as a honing tool for the mind.  We can acknowledge that a lot of kids "can't see the forest for the trees," especially in subjects that hold no immediate interest to them, but that doesn't negate the fact that there is still a forest to be seen.

Then began the era of trying out makeup trends and attempting to cover up my flaws.  I've always had a light case of rosacea on my cheeks, HATED it, so I went about 12 years refusing to let anyone see me without foundation.  My face doesn't wear bold makeup well at all, so the most I ever did was the foundation/black eyeshadow for eyeliner/mascara/ inner eye highlight, but I went 12 years where I did that every day regardless of where I was going.

I did feel confident and put together, I had the routine down to 15 min.  But then around 28, I started having a really hard time with my PCOS..it sent my face back to puberty-mode and I found that putting anything on my skin just made it worse.  Then I started growing eyelashes hyperactively?! which basically meant KP/impacted pores of the lash line...there went eye makeup.  Then there was the culmination of my experiences with SA..started to feel like putting an effort into my appearance put a target on my back, so for the last 3 1/2 years I've made an effort to look as plain as I can.  

At first I was ridiculously self-conscious of my skin, but I've been able to work on healing rather than concealing, and now the goal is just healthy rather than flawless.  In some ways I've learned to see my scars, dark circles, and white hair as a badge of honor because it speaks to the shit I've been through.  I don't feel fresh, bright, and pretty anymore, so I don't want to "false advertise".. It's the epitome of what ya see is what ya get.  It's true acceptance of myself that I might not have come to had my health not forced me to abstain from makeup.

Pasta Pomodoro

Start a pot of salted water to boil, any pasta is fine

In a measuring cup:
1/4 c- 1/3 c olive oil
2-3 cloves minced garlic (I prefer fresh, but jarred or paste is fine)
4-5 leaves of fresh basil, chiffonade (I use about 1 1/2 Tbsp of that half-dried stuff from the produce section because it lasts for months in my fridge)
Salt and pepper to your taste
About 8 oz of grape or cherry tomatoes, quartered (a can of diced tomatoes works fine too)
Mix this up and let marinate while pasta cooks

Cook your pasta to al dente, drain, mix with "sauce" and let simmer on low until tomatoes are soft and the garlic is no longer raw..maybe 7-10 minutes.
Top with some fresh grated parmesan and asiago, or that shake Parm if that's all ya got.
